AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Overweight and obesity are both in Europe and in Spain, one of the major public health problems since they are associated with cardiovascular risk factors and the occurrence of other diseases. Nowadays, the prevalence of obesity SEEDO in Spanish society is about 25%. In addition to evaluating how our lifestyle habits influence in our weight, it would be interesting to assess how the festivity days, which in many cases are often extended beyond officially holidays, can influence the total annual weight gain.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A prospective and descriptive study was conducted in a total of 258 patients (95 men and 163 women) undergoing a treatment for weight reduction, at least during one month ago. We studied seven holiday periods.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: In all patients, there was a significant linear correlation (p < 0.05) difference between weight loss and vacational time studied with greater prevalence in the Christmas period. No statistically significant association was found between weight loss and age or sex.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Prospective study on the effect of the influence of holiday periods in the weight during a low-calory dietetic treatment].
Article.VernacularTitle: Estudio prospectivo del efecto del periodo vacacional sobre la influencia del peso durante el tratamiento dietoterapeútico hipocalórico.

Según la SEEDO la prevalencia de obesidad en la sociedad española está cerca del 25 %. Además del estudio de nuestro estilo de vida y hábitos incorporados a las costumbres cotidianas, resultaría interesante evaluar cómo influyen en la ganancia de peso total anual los excesos realizados durante muchas festividades, que en muchos casos se suelen prolongar más allá de los días oficialmente festivos.
